title: Camera-trap distance sampling of Maxwell's duikers at 21 cameras in Taï National Park, Côte d'Ivoire, 2014: peak-activity hours
creator: Howe, Eric J.; Buckland, Stephen T.; Després-Einspenner, Marie-Lyne; Kühl, Hjalmar S.
citation: Howe, E. J., Buckland, S. T., Després-Einspenner, M.-L., & Kühl, H. S. (2018). Data from: Distance sampling with camera traps [Dataset]. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.b4c70
abstract: Maxwell's duikers (Philantomba maxwellii) filmed by 21 camera traps in Taï National Park, Côte d'Ivoire, in 2014, for the first application of point-transect distance sampling to camera traps (Howe et al. 2017). At each 2-second snapshot a filmed duiker was assigned to a distance interval from the camera (11 intervals from 1 to 21 m). This table covers the hours of peak duiker activity: one row per camera x distance interval, y = snapshot detections in the interval over the deployment, with the camera's temporal effort (2-s steps) and position.
samplingProtocol: Camera traps (42-degree field of view) recording video; duikers in view at 2-second snapshot moments assigned to distance intervals from reference markers; effort = number of 2-s steps operated during the hours analysed.
surveyEvidenceNote: Every camera appears in the file; a camera with no detection in the hours covered has a single row with no distance (3 here). Each camera has a row in every distance interval (0 where nothing was recorded).
closureNote: occasion (distance intervals of one camera deployment)
geographicCoverage: Taï National Park, south-western Côte d'Ivoire (about 5.82 N, 7.27 W); camera positions as unit_decimalLatitude/Longitude
crs: EPSG:4326, converted from the deposit's UTM 29N metres (EPSG:32629)

coordinatesCoarsened.method: camera positions as published (UTM metres, converted); Philantomba maxwellii is IUCN Least Concern

notes: Distance intervals inferred from the deposited midpoints (help page: 'recorded distances are the midpoints of the intervals'): (1,2], ..., (7,8], (8,10], (10,12], (12,15], (15,21] m; nothing is recorded within 1 m. y counts snapshot detections (a duiker seen at several 2-s steps counts at each), as in the paper's camera-trap distance sampling. Area 40.37 km2 and the field-of-view multiplier 42/360 are constants of the deposit. Sibling: howe_2017_tai_duiker_ds (all daytime hours). This peak subset is the Distance package's DuikerCameraTraps.
